title: console: a user with no stored language who picked 中文 on the sign-in page sees English month names in date cells on every load, because the Accept-Language answer outranks the UI language
body:
domain:ui#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CY2n1JmZZKrHgtp9jC

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location and a reproduction. Found by the #27498 dev (card thread on branch `claude/project-thread-b2omyd`, PR #27624, os-dev-report 6500538340) while reproducing #27498. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets lane and grade. PR #27624 fixes the language-switch race and does not close this.

**Business reason.** A Chinese-speaking user whose `sys_user.locale` was never written (they chose 中文 on the sign-in page, not through the avatar menu) sees every list grid's dates as `Nov 18` / `Oct 11` under Chinese headers, on every page load, while the UI language is Chinese. Dates read as foreign text in the one place a user scans them most.

## Measured (dev's reproduction on `examples/app-showcase`)

- `sys_user.locale` unset, device/sign-in language zh: `GET /api/v1/auth/me/localization` answers the `Accept-Language` rung, and `ui/packages/i18n/src/useDisplayLocale.ts` (~L64-68) returns `localization.locale || language || 'en'`, so the server's answer outranks the active UI language. The grid's 截止日期 column reads `Nov 18` on every load.

## Wanted (design call, not decided here)

Which source wins for display formatting when the user never chose a language: the server's request-derived answer, or the UI language the user picked on the sign-in page. Changing `useDisplayLocale`'s precedence touches every date/number renderer; a server-side answer (marking an `Accept-Language`-derived locale as such) is the other route.

## Dedupe

Open `domain:ui` titles read for `locale`, `language`, `month`, `Accept-Language`: only #27498 (the switch race, PR #27624). **New.**
